questions.q: In the order-processing API review, what makes 'This design has no failure domain isolation above the pod level' a strong reliability finding?
options: It names the exact gap (no secondary region or failover automation) and implies the direction of the fix
It proves the cluster will never go down
It recommends switching from AKS to EKS
It is phrased as a general concern without pointing to a specific gap
questions.explain: A strong pillar finding names the specific gap and points toward what fixing it would require — here, a secondary region and tested failover.

questions.q: The review found the API's managed identity has subscription-level Contributor access and the database accepts traffic from the full subnet. Which pillar does this finding belong to, and why?
options: Cost optimization, because over-permissioned identities increase licensing cost
Performance efficiency, because broad permissions slow down API calls
Reliability, because permissions affect uptime
Security, because it's an over-permissioned identity and a wider-than-necessary network trust boundary
questions.explain: Over-permissioned access and an overly broad network boundary are textbook security-pillar findings — least privilege and trust-boundary scoping.

questions.q: The cluster is provisioned for Black Friday peak load year-round, at roughly 4x average Tuesday demand. What does the lesson say a careful cost optimization finding should NOT assume?
options: That the compute should be deleted entirely
That the headroom is automatically wasteful — it might be a deliberate reliability tradeoff worth examining, not an automatic cut
That autoscaling is misconfigured and must be disabled
That the finding applies to the database tier only, never compute
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly cautions that oversized headroom might be a deliberate reliability tradeoff — a cost finding shouldn't assume it's pure waste without checking that intent.

questions.q: Which of these is described in the lesson as an operational excellence finding for the order-processing API?
options: The database accepts connections from the full subnet
No autoscaling minimum is configured
There is no documented on-call routing, rollback procedure, or alert threshold for the workload
Node SKU is mismatched to the workload's CPU-bound profile
questions.explain: Operational excellence findings are about who owns running the system day to day — on-call routing, rollback procedures, and alert thresholds, as described in the lesson.

questions.q: What is the key takeaway from seeing all five pillar findings produced against the same architecture in one review?
options: Only the reliability finding actually matters; the rest are secondary
Each pillar's finding can be independently true at the same time, and fixing all five together is where real tradeoffs start to surface
A design that fails any single pillar should be scrapped entirely
The five findings always contradict each other and cannot all be addressed
questions.explain: The lesson's closing point is that distinct, independently valid findings across all five pillars can coexist — and reconciling fixes across them is exactly the tradeoff work covered next.
